In order to have a proper discussion about the pricing of ports you need to pose an argument with video games that have similar circumstances. Using Crash as your argument against the pricing of the port of DKTF is easy to pick apart. Crash is available on 4 different platforms, each with varying market shares. Crash is priced at $40 because the PC/PS4/XBONE markets are much larger. The MSRP was set at this price likely because they determined that the game would not be able to compete as well in all four of those different markets had it been set at $60. 

Now I know DKTF was initially $50 upon release and is now $20 as a select title, but there’s a reason why it wasn’t $60 in the first place. The game released in Q1 of 2014 after being delayed from Q4 of 2013. The game was delayed most likely due to financial reporting concerns. Q1 of 2014 was bleak as hell. DKTF was literally the only game in vast sea of nothing being offered from Nintendo at the time. They needed DKTF to be released in Q1 of 2014 (and not Q4 of 2013 which already had Super Mario 3D World and A Link Between Worlds propping it up) and they needed to have the game sell *in that quarter*. So the reason why it was likely $50 from the start is because they desperately needed to incentivize buyers into picking up the game sooner than later. 

So with that information in mind, to answer your question, they can sell DKTF at $60 now because they can. Bottom line. And it’s selling like crazy. It was the number one game in Japan in the month of May and it’s outselling the Wii U version - no contest. This is simple economics. The game is priced in accordance with the consumers willingness to pay, and apparently consumers are willing to pay. Price drop? Not happening. This game will probably be $60 for years to come. This game can not be found on PS4, XBONE or PC *and* it doesn’t have to share it’s market share with nearly as many third parties as Crash on 4 different markets. 

Disclaimer: I am in no way defending Nintendo. I am simply answering your question with the hard truth. For the record, I own DKTF on the Wii U. Bought it on release day in 2014. I also want to have it on my Switch, but not for $60.
